minutes.headline: Commission approved Hickory Hills' five-year lake order of conditions, and continued four Northfield/Holman house filings.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission approved the Lake Shirley weed treatment plan, several small determinations, and the Hickory Hills Lake order of conditions after a long line-by-line review. Four Ed McSweeney house applications were continued to August 3 over unresolved wetland delineation, and the Haas driveway filing was continued to August 17. The commission also asked the select board to consider litigation over encroachments at two Woodland Drive properties.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether public notice of the Lake Shirley treatment had gone out, and whether weekly data is provided.
Said the Haas driveway extends onto her land, with concerns about runoff to the marsh and removal of vegetation.

Hickory Hills representatives (Paula Bertram, John, Nicole Waters) commented on the draft order of conditions: monitoring frequency, newspaper notice, fan wort treatment speed, diver-assisted suction harvesting.
Asked what remediation is required in the 30-foot buffer and said he was never notified of earlier hearings.

budget_items.what_was_said: The administrator suggested developing budgets for the revolving accounts so reimbursements can be processed through the accounting system rather than by the town accountant.
A member is getting window and sliding door replacement quotes and working with the tenant to document expenses for reimbursement.
Hickory Hills noted a cost to newspaper notices and asked that they be dropped.

decisions.decision: Four McSweeney NOIs held until a new wetlands delineation with field notes is supplied; applicant urged to check eligibility of the consultant named.
Commission agreed to drop the local newspaper notice requirement from the Hickory Hills conditions.
Algae monitoring language to be made generic, tied to the lake management plan, rather than detailed in conditions.
Field change at 238 Fire Road 16 to use the New England wildlife conservation mix, not clover.
Chair to consult the land use director before the commission considers a donation of land at 360 New West Townsend Road.
Commission to visit 411 Goodrich Street during site visits around July 30; timing to be arranged by email.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved the Hickory Hills Lake order of conditions after a long line-by-line review.
The commission approved herbicide treatment of Little Hickory, and earlier approved the Lake Shirley weed treatment plan.
Four McSweeney house filings on Northfield Road and Holman Street were continued to August 3 until a new wetlands delineation with field notes is supplied.
The commission voted to ask the select board to consider litigation over encroachments at 104 and 116 Woodland Drive.
The Haas driveway filing on Townsend Harbor Road was continued to August 17 after an abutter raised runoff and vegetation concerns.

why_it_matters: The Hickory Hills order sets the monitoring and treatment conditions for a lake's five-year management plan, which affects lake users and abutters.
The Woodland Drive request moves a possible enforcement dispute over buffer encroachments to the select board, which could be asked to authorize legal action.
watch_next: August 3 continued hearings: four McSweeney filings and two Proctor filings, with the new wetlands delineation
August 17 continued hearing on the Haas driveway filing

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on 14 of the 15 votes: the same motions, the same continuance dates and unanimous roll calls.
